title: Getting to Maneybhanjan and Out from Rimbik
meta_description: How to reach the Sandakphu trek: NJP or Bagdogra to Darjeeling or Mirik, shared jeeps to Maneybhanjan, car fares, and the way out from Srikhola and Rimbik.
summary: Take a train to New Jalpaiguri (NJP) or fly to Bagdogra, ride a shared jeep up to Darjeeling for ₹250–350, then another to Maneybhanjan, 26 km away, for ₹100–150. A reserved car from NJP straight to Maneybhanjan costs ₹3,500–4,500. Most treks end at Srikhola or Rimbik, with early shared jeeps back to Darjeeling.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Maneybhanjan, the small border town where every Sandakphu trek begins, sits 26 km west of Darjeeling on the road through Ghoom and Sukhiapokhri. Nobody gets there in one hop from the plains without paying for it. The cheapest way is two shared jeeps: NJP or Siliguri to Darjeeling, then Darjeeling to Maneybhanjan. The quickest is a reserved car from NJP or Bagdogra straight to the trailhead, about 3.5–4 hours.

Most trekkers spend the night before in Darjeeling, which makes sense for two reasons. It gives a day at 2,000 m before the climb to the ridge, which helps the body adjust, and it lets you start from Maneybhanjan by 8 or 9 am, register with the park, meet your guide and still reach Tumling before dark. All fares below are indicative for 2025–26; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: From the plains to Darjeeling
paras: New Jalpaiguri (NJP) is the main railhead, with overnight trains from Kolkata, such as the Darjeeling Mail and Padatik Express, and long-distance trains from Delhi, Guwahati and the south. Bagdogra airport, about 14 km west of Siliguri, has direct flights from Kolkata, Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and other cities.

Shared jeeps for Darjeeling wait outside NJP station and at the stands on Hill Cart Road in Siliguri, and leave when full from early morning until mid-afternoon. A seat costs about ₹250–350 and the ride takes 3–3.5 hours. From Bagdogra, most people take a taxi to Siliguri (about ₹400–600) and pick up a jeep there, or book a reserved car straight up. The toy train from NJP to Darjeeling is a fine ride, but at 7–8 hours or more it is not a trekking transfer, and services change, so check current status before you travel.

If you prefer to skip Darjeeling, a quieter route runs from Siliguri up through Mirik and Sukhiapokhri to Maneybhanjan. Shared jeeps from Siliguri to Mirik are frequent; onward connections to Sukhiapokhri and Maneybhanjan are fewer and need more patience.

sections.heading: Darjeeling to Maneybhanjan
paras: Shared jeeps to Maneybhanjan leave from the motor stand below Chowk Bazaar in Darjeeling through the morning. Some run direct; others go to Sukhiapokhri, where you change for the last few kilometres. Ask at the counter the evening before for the first departure, and aim to be on a jeep by 7 or 7.30 am. The road climbs to Ghoom, then follows the ridge west through Lepchajagat and Sukhiapokhri before dropping to Maneybhanjan, about 26 km in 1–1.5 hours.

Groups of four with packs often find a reserved car, at ₹1,500–2,000, worth the small extra, because it can leave at 6.30 am and stop where you want. Ask the driver to drop you at the guide and park office area rather than the jeep stand, so you can start your paperwork at once.

sections.heading: What to do at Maneybhanjan
paras: Maneybhanjan is a short bazaar street on a saddle, with the border to Nepal marked by a small culvert in the middle of it. Everything you need before the trek is within a few hundred metres. Allow 45–90 minutes here in season.
list: Meet your guide or engage one at the guide office; a licensed guide is compulsory inside Singalila National Park for every group.
Pay park entry and any camera fee, and register names, ID numbers and your planned route.
If you are riding, settle the Land Rover rate, route and number of nights with the owners' association counter.
Buy last snacks, batteries and toilet paper; shops past Maneybhanjan are small and dearer.
Show photo ID if asked: Indians carry a passport or voter ID, foreigners a passport with a valid Indian visa. The rules at border posts change, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Starting at Dhotrey instead
paras: Not every trek starts at Maneybhanjan bazaar. Dhotrey, a forest village at about 2,500 m on the eastern slope of the ridge, is about an hour by jeep beyond Maneybhanjan, and a forest trail of about 6 km climbs from there to Tonglu at 3,070 m. It is the shortest walking route onto the ridge, and it never crosses into Nepal.

Shared jeeps from Maneybhanjan to Dhotrey run less often than those from Darjeeling, at about ₹80–150 a seat; a reserved jeep costs about ₹1,200–1,800, and a reserved car from Darjeeling about ₹2,500–3,500. You still pay park entry and take on your guide at Maneybhanjan on the way. Families with children, older walkers and anyone short of time often start here, spend a night in a Dhotrey homestay, and climb to Tonglu fresh the next morning.
From Tonglu the route joins the main trail at Tumling, a few minutes away, and carries on to Gairibas, Kalipokhri and Sandakphu as usual.

sections.heading: Getting out: Srikhola and Rimbik
paras: Most walking treks end on the eastern side of the ridge. The short route drops from Sandakphu to Srikhola via Gurdum; the long one continues to Phalut and comes down through Gorkhey, Samanden and Rammam. Either way, the jeep road now reaches Srikhola, and from there it is 30–45 minutes on to Rimbik, the market village where shared jeeps for Darjeeling start.

Rimbik's shared jeeps leave early, often between 6 and 7.30 am, with fewer later in the day. The 56 km ride back to Darjeeling takes 4–5 hours on winding roads. If you finish at Srikhola late in the afternoon, spend the night there or in Rimbik and take the morning jeep. Departure times vary by season and day of the week, so ask your guide to confirm the evening before; check current status before you travel.
Some trekkers who walk up to Sandakphu ride back down. Your guide can arrange a Land Rover back to Maneybhanjan, which brings you out on the Darjeeling side in about three hours.

If you prefer not to sit in a crowded jeep for five hours after a week of walking, groups of four or five can share a reserved jeep from Rimbik and ask the driver to stop for lunch on the way. It also lets you go straight down to Siliguri or NJP, which takes most of a day.

sections.heading: Timing your arrival and departure
paras: Build slack into both ends of the trip. A landslide on the Darjeeling road, a jeep that fills slowly or one foggy morning on the ridge can each cost half a day.
list: Arrive in Darjeeling the day before the trek, not on the morning you start walking.
Plan to leave the hills a day before any flight or long train, or at least leave Rimbik by 7 am for an evening train from NJP.
Avoid starting on a Saturday in October if you can; lodges at Tumling fill fastest at weekends.
In the monsoon shoulder weeks, ask about road conditions on the Rimbik and Mirik routes before you set out.
Keep the guide's phone number and the Land Rover association counter number saved, since plans change with weather.

faqs.q: How do I reach Maneybhanjan from NJP?
faqs.a: Take a shared jeep from NJP or Siliguri to Darjeeling, about ₹250–350 a seat and 3–3.5 hours, then a shared jeep from Darjeeling's Chowk Bazaar motor stand to Maneybhanjan, about ₹100–150 and 1–1.5 hours. A reserved car from NJP straight to Maneybhanjan costs about ₹3,500–4,500 and takes 3.5–4 hours. Fares are indicative; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Maneybhanjan from Darjeeling?
faqs.a: About 26 km by road, via Ghoom, Lepchajagat and Sukhiapokhri. Shared jeeps take 1–1.5 hours and cost about ₹100–150 a seat, leaving from the motor stand below Chowk Bazaar through the morning. A reserved car costs about ₹1,500–2,000. Start early so you can register at the park office and reach Tumling before dark.

faqs.q: Which airport is nearest to Sandakphu?
faqs.a: Bagdogra, about 14 km west of Siliguri, is the nearest airport, with direct flights from Kolkata, Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and other cities. From Bagdogra to Maneybhanjan is about 3.5–4 hours by reserved car, roughly ₹3,500–4,500. Budget travellers take a taxi to Siliguri and shared jeeps via Darjeeling, which takes longer but costs far less.

faqs.q: Can I go from Siliguri to Maneybhanjan without going to Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Yes, via Mirik and Sukhiapokhri. Shared jeeps run often from Siliguri to Mirik; from there you need connections to Sukhiapokhri and Maneybhanjan, which are fewer. A reserved car on this route takes about 3.5–4 hours. Most trekkers still prefer a night in Darjeeling for the extra acclimatisation and easy morning jeeps.

faqs.q: How do I get back to Darjeeling after the Sandakphu trek?
faqs.a: Most treks end at Srikhola or Rimbik. From Srikhola, take a jeep to Rimbik, about 30–45 minutes, then a morning shared jeep to Darjeeling, about 4–5 hours and ₹200–300 a seat. A reserved jeep from Rimbik costs about ₹3,000–4,500. Departure times vary, so confirm the evening before.

faqs.q: What time do jeeps leave Rimbik for Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Mostly early, between about 6 and 7.30 am, with fewer departures later in the day. Times change with the season and the day of the week, so ask your guide or lodge the evening before. If you arrive at Srikhola late, spend the night there or at Rimbik and take the morning jeep. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Should I stay in Darjeeling before the Sandakphu trek?
faqs.a: Yes, we recommend one night. Darjeeling, at about 2,050 m, gives the body a day at altitude before you climb toward 3,000 m on day one. It also puts you on an early jeep so you can finish paperwork at Maneybhanjan and reach Tumling in daylight. Hostels and budget lodges in town are easy to find outside peak weeks.

faqs.q: Can I take the toy train to the Sandakphu trek?
faqs.a: Not practically. The toy train from NJP to Darjeeling takes 7–8 hours or more and does not go to Maneybhanjan. It is a fine ride in its own right, so some trekkers take it on a spare day before or after. Services and timetables change often; check current status before you travel and book on IRCTC.

faqs.q: What ID do I need to start the Sandakphu trek?
faqs.a: Indian citizens should carry a passport or voter ID, which SSB and Nepal police may check where the trail crosses into Nepal. Foreign nationals need a passport with a valid Indian visa. You will also register ID details at the park office in Maneybhanjan. The rules on accepted ID change, so check current status before you travel.
